#2651. 10 Takeaways from another Celtics NBA Cup win over Wizards

It felt like Jayson Tatum was due to have a big game coming into this matchup and he delivered, finishing with a season-high 41 points, 8 assists,6 rebounds, and 2 blocks on 13-25 shooting from the field and 6-15 shooting from three. Tatum put on an absolute masterclass in the first half, with 28 points and all 6 of his three pointers.

The Wizards defense seemed to have the game plan of just putting Alex Sarr on an island and he got cooked. Tatum spent the entire first half just raining down threes and the Wizards had no way of stopping it. Just look at the way his eyes lit up when he saw Sarr was trying to defend him.

In the second half, we saw Tatum struggle with shooting the ball again (4-12 FG, 0-6 3PM), but I would say he still did a great job on offense. He was able to get to the basket with relative ease and did a good job getting to the free throw line. The only concern had to be the free throw shooting, finishing 9-14. I don't even remember the last time we saw him miss 5 free throws in a game, but even he said in his postgame interview that he wasn't happy with his second half performance and left some points on the board.

Either way, this game might not go down as his best performance, but it will still go down as his 2nd 40-point game of the season and the 31st time he has done it in his NBA Career. That is second in Boston Celtics history, only behind Larry Bird who did it 47 times.

I don't know what it is about playing games on NBC that turns Paul George into one of the best players in the league. George finished with 28 points and 9 assists on 11-20 shooting from the field and 6-9 shooting from three.

Similar to Tatum, George was absolutely incredible when it came to his three-point shooting in this game. Washington's defense just could not stop Boston's offense in the first half. In the second quarter alone, George dropped 13 points. He hit some absurd shots in this game and it just looked effortless, like in the beginning of the second quarter when he hit back-to-back threes, one on a silky step-back and the other on a pull-up that caused Washington to call timeout.

The best highlight of the night for George came in his 12-point third quarter performance. When Kyshawn George tried to play 1-on-1 defense midway through the quarter, Paul George hit him with a mean crossover that sent him falling down. Paul then paused and splashed the mid-range jumper for one of the nastiest ankle-breakers we've seen all season.

Sadly, the Celtics don't have another game scheduled on NBC until December 28th against the Cavaliers, so we will have to wait a little bit until we get another NBC PG game.

Coming into this game, I was interested to see how Neemias Queta would match up against the Wizards front court with Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr, but Queta absolutely feasted like it was Thanksgiving. He finished with a season-high 21 points on 9-11 shooting along with 5 rebounds and 2 blocks.

Queta's first quarter was some of the best basketball we have ever seen out of him, finishing with 13 points on 6-7 shooting — he was just getting anything he wanted. He scored 8 of the Celtics first 13 points coming on attacking the basket with force. Queta was able to get behind the Wizards defense on almost every roll, with Tatum and George finding him alley-oops and easy finishes.

With a new season high of 17 points set in the first half, Queta did get into foul trouble in the third quarter and didn't play a lot of minutes in the second half. You could tell the Celtics were thrown all out of whack without Queta on the floor, furthering the importance of his impact when he is out there. It was really cool to see them feed Queta in this game and I just love watching him on the court.

After scoring 80 points in the first half, it felt like the Celtics were finally getting back to normal. They already have one of the best NBA Cup point differentials ever and there was a chance it could have gone up exponentially in the second half but it didn't work out that way. Washington outscored Boston 40-24, shooting 13-20 (65%) from the field and 5-10 (50%) from three. The Celtics on the other hand shot 9-22 (40.9%) from the field and 3-9 (33.3) from three.

All credit to the Wizards for showing fight, but it just was not a good look for the Celtics, especially since on their four-game losing streak, the second half offense falling off was a huge problem. Luckily for Boston, the lead was big enough to where the Wizards couldn't make a full comeback, but it was still a nightmare third quarter. The defense looked lackadaisical and the open shots that were falling early in the game just stopped.

The fourth quarter was even worse shooting wise (8-27 FG, 4-16 3PM) but at least they were able to generate some stops on defense in the end. This second half performance shifted the entire vibe about this game. I hate to say it, but there were times where it genuinely felt like Boston was going to blow this lead. It is not a great feeling that you are almost waiting for it to happen, but this last stretch of games have not instilled much confidence.

With under three minutes left in the game, the Wizards cut the Celtics deficit to 7 points and they had all the momentum. Boston was looking for someone to come through and stop the bleeding and they got an unlikely hero in Baylor Scheierman. Going into the fourth quarter, Scheierman had yet to score and wasn't looking to be aggressive for most of this game.

With 2:31 left, Jayson Tatum was doubled on the block and found Scheierman for a deep three that pushed the Celtics lead back up to 10. This was a huge basket for Boston, but he wasn't done. After an Anthony Davis miss, Derrick White missed a three and Scheierman drew a foul on Trae Young during the offensive rebound to get to free throws where he made both. Young would make a layup on the next possession, but Scheierman would follow it with his second three in a row off a nice behind the back pass from Tatum, forcing a Washington timeout.

That 8-2 run by Scheierman completely changed the trajectory of this game. If he didn't hit those shots, it felt like Washington was going to find a way to tie or even take the lead. He benefitted greatly from the gravity Tatum created for him and did not hesitate when it came to shooting the big shots. It shows how much confidence Scheierman has now and the trust Joe Mazzulla has in him to put him in this situation.

For the 11th time this season, Joe Mazzulla has put out a brand-new starting lineup. This time the Celtics went with Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta. This is the third game in a row Hauser has started, replacing Jordan Walsh in the opening lineup. Coming into this game, this lineup had only played 9 minutes together but had a net rating of +46.8 with an offensive rating of 136.8 and defensive rating of 90.0.

This lineup looked to be, according to the numbers, the best option for the Celtics to go with and felt fitting they tried it here. This starting lineup would proceed to open this game on a 17-9 run, giving Boston a spark that the offensive desperately needed. With more of a sample size of 26 minutes, Boston has a net rating of +52.2 with an offensive rating of 146.3 and a defensive rating of 94.1.

For as much as I like the idea of a guy like Walsh or Hugo Gonzalez in the starting lineup to defend the best player, I do think Hauser is the best choice when it comes to the offensive upside of this team. I hope we see this lineup get more minutes moving forward because it feels like the Celtics have found something that really works here.

Celtics starting lineup stats (Via databallr)

Maybe the biggest story of the Celtics losing streak was how bad their shooting was three-point range. Over those 4 games, Boston shot 68-for-205 (33.2%) from the perimeter, but this game was a refreshing change of pace as Boston finished shooting 22-51 (43.1%) against the Wizards. However, even this number can be a little bit misleading.

In the first half, the Celtics could not miss from beyond the arc, shooting 15-26 (57.7%). This was aided due to the fact that it felt like the Wizards were leaving them wide open on almost every attempt and it looked like all the frustration from the last four games were coming out all at once. Then the second half hit and Boston's shooting started to mirror what they've been doing, finishing 7-25 (28%). Washington didn't necessarily change their defensive game plan, giving Boston the same open threes but the Celtics just weren't knocking them down.

It is encouraging that Boston did hit 22 threes in this game, showcasing the elite form they were playing with earlier in the season. I am still concerned with the second half shooting continuing to drop off. This trend is due to the lack of rim pressure the Celtics have on the roster. Outside of Tatum, who consistently gets a lot of their points when it comes to attacking the basket? This results in the Celtics taking all of these threes and if they aren't falling, it will lead to losses. This is not a new problem by any means, it just seems to be a more glaring issue during this rough patch in the season.

The Celtics free throw shooting is not normally an issue that we have had to worry about in years past but to start this season we have seen Boston shoot very poorly at the charity stripe. Boston is ranked 24th in the NBA at 75.8%. There were a lot of misses in this game as the Celtics shot 17-25 from the line. Tatum missed 5 free throws in this game alone and although it didn't hurt them, we have seen it cost Boston games a few times already.

On the Celtics four game losing streak, we saw them lose almost every game at the free throw line. Against the Magic, they missed 8 free throws and lost by 10, against the Nuggets they missed 2 free throws and lost by 4, against the Kings they missed 10 free throws and lost by 1, and finally against the Warriors they missed 3 free throws and lost by 1.

With the 1st pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, the Washington Wizards selected Brockton, MA native AJ Dybantsa form BYU. Dybantsa for years has been in the zeitgeist of the NBA world and even the Celtics to an extent. Dybantsa has been a well known Celtics fan for a long time now and last season he played against UConn in TD Garden for the first time. In this game it was the first time he played against his hometown team and he showed out.

Dybantsa finished with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and 7 assists on 7-16 shooting from the field and 2-6 from three. He was incredibly explosive when it came to attacking the basket and even hit some big time shots running the offense for Washington in the fourth quarter. It was cool to see a kid from Massachusetts make it big to the NBA and he gave the Celtics a pretty good fight. In his postgame press conference he was asked how it felt to face off against his childhood team and he said, "I've been a Celtics fan since I came out the womb."

I hate to play conspiracy theorist, but it sounds like we could be seeing AJ in a Celtics jersey at some point in his NBA career. Just wait until he teams up well fellow New England star Cooper Flagg in 2035. It will be special hoops. Jokes aside, I think Dybantsa will have a great NBA career and will be thorn in the Celtics side in Eastern Conference battles to come. He will surely get a big standing ovation when the Wizards come to TD Garden for a mini two-game series on December 14th and 16th.

When it comes to the NBA Cup, no one has been better than the Boston Celtics this season. They are currently 3-0 in the standings with an incredible +69 point differential. This was aided from two blowouts against the Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets but even the 15 point win against Washington makes them look even more impressive. The second best team according to point differential is the San Antonio Spurs at +53.

With the Celtics win in this game, they have a 99.9% chance of making it to the next round of the NBA Cup ahead of their last matchup against the Atlanta Hawks on Friday. If they win, they will be the number one seed in the Cup Playoffs and get home court advantage. If they lose by less than 40 points, they would end up as the four seed.

We have seen multiple players on this team talk about how they really want to win the NBA Cup this year. Sam Hauser talked about the thrilling matchup between the Knicks and Spurs last season and both of those teams made the NBA Finals. Neemias Queta also said he likes the idea of the NBA Cup and talked about how the Celtics had never made it very far and they have used that as motivation this season. If the numbers didn't already show it, Boston looks to be taking the NBA Cup very seriously and could potentially find themselves taking a trip to Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indiana for the Championship Game.

#2650. Aaron Rodgers Claims He Found Out About Steelers Benching from Teammate

Aaron Rodgers says he learned of his sudden benching from the Pittsburgh Steelers from a teammate

He said Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth broke the news on a phone call Nov. 24, the same night the team shared the news widely

Rodgers recalled the call while breaking his silence and sharing that his time with the Steelers is over on The Pat McAfee Show on Nov. 25

Fans learned Aaron Rodgers is no longer the Pittsburgh Steelers' starting quarterback on social media. He says he got the news from a teammate.

The 42-year-old quarterback recalled the moment he learned he would be inactive for the Steelers' next game during a surprise appearance Wednesday, Nov. 25 on The Pat McAfee Show. Rodgers, who previously said he would retire at the end of the season, claimed he learned the news of his status from tight end Pat Freiermuth before leveling a handful of accusations at head coach Mike McCarthy.

"I found out that I was going to be inactive on a phone call last night with Pat Freiermuth," the NFL star told host Pat McAfee and co-host A.J. Hawk on Wednesday's program.

Head coach Mike McCarthy talks with Aaron Rodgers in September 2026Credit: Joe Sargent/Getty

"I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know," Rodgers continued. "And he told me, and obviously there had been a lot of things in motion at that point."

The four-time NFL MVP said that his removal from the starting position never came up in conversation with McCarthy — who coached Rodgers for more than a decade in Green Bay — prior to the benching.

"I didn't hear from Mike," Rodgers claimed, adding the two last spoke around 6 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 24. "Still haven't heard from people over there," Rodgers said, adding his agents "obviously talked with" Steelers general manager Omar Khan.

"Yeah, the way it was released last night, and like trying to get out and ahead, like there was some benching going on… Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, that word never even came up," Rodgers said.

On Wednesday in the Steelers' locker room, Freiermuth said he "was just checking in on a close friend" when asked about the call with Rodgers.

The Steelers did not immediately return PEOPLE's request for comment.

The Steelers announced the quarterback change late Tuesday night.

"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos," Steelers spokesperson Burt Lauten said in the statement. "Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday."

Less than 24 hours later, reports emerged the team is expected to release Rodgers.

#2647. ‘Definitely a cool moment’: AJ Dybantsa shines in front of his childhood-favorite Celtics

AJ Dybantsa grew up in Brockton, Mass., about 30 minutes away from TD Garden, rooting for the Celtics his entire life.

On Tuesday night, the 19-year-old Wizards rookie hosted them in Washington's NBA Cup group finale. The Celtics won, 131-116, but it was a night Dybantsa won't soon forget.

"Definitely a cool moment," Dybantsa told reporters in Washington. "I've been a Celtics fan since I came out the womb. I was born in Boston, been going to Celtics games since I was two years old, wearing Kevin Garnett's jersey, then Paul Pierce's jersey to Isaiah Thomas', all the way to [Jayson] Tatum and [Jaylen] Brown."

Before Dybantsa committed to BYU, became a collegiate superstar, and went No. 1 in the 2026 NBA Draft, he attended Tatum's basketball camp. Back then, he was a youth prospect just starting to build buzz at Saint Sebastian's School in Needham, Mass., before transferring to Prolific Prep in Napa, Calif., and once more to Utah Prep Academy in Hurricane, Utah.

Tatum took the time to get to know Dybantsa and share some advice. So when the two crossed paths again, this time as fellow professionals, Dybantsa was struck by the moment. He did, however, admit it could be even bigger when they meet for the rematch on Dec. 14 at TD Garden.

"I think it'll be more surreal when I play over there, but today was definitely a cool moment," Dybantsa said.

WASHINGTON, DC – NOVEMBER 24: AJ Dybantsa #4 of the Washington Wizards plays defense during the game against the Boston Celtics as part of the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 24, 2026 at Capital One Arena in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Stephen Gosling/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

It won't be the first time Dybantsa has played on Boston's parquet.

Last season at BYU, Dybantsa won over the crowd as a freshman facing No. 3 UConn at TD Garden. He relished the homecoming, scoring 25 points (including 21 in the second half) with six rebounds and two steals in an 86-84 loss to the Huskies. Jaylen Brown and Derrick White sat courtside, watching New England rally behind one of its own on his way to the NBA.

Nearly a year later, Dybantsa put on a show to win over Washington's crowd, finishing with 20 points, 11 rebounds and a career-high seven assists against the No. 2 seed Celtics.

Dybantsa is averaging 20 points, 9.2 rebounds and 4.8 assists on 45.6 percent shooting over his last five games. He shot 7-for-18 on Tuesday night and knocked down a pair of threes, which, to Tatum, is just a sneak peek of what's to come in the near future from Dybantsa.

"The sky's the limit for him," Tatum told reporters. "[He's] somebody that I met a long time ago when he was a kid and got to know him pretty well. He was at my first Elite Camp. I know his father pretty well, so he has a really, really bright future."

Tatum put on a show himself, eager to get Boston back in the win column amid its four-game losing streak.

He dropped 41 points with six rebounds and eight assists, his 31st career 40-point game. That moved him into second place on the Celtics' all-time list, behind only Larry Bird (47).

WASHINGTON, DC – NOVEMBER 24: Paul George #13 of the Boston Celtics and AJ Dybantsa #4 of the Washington Wizards talk after the game as part of the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 24, 2026 at Capital One Arena in Washington, DC. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Stephen Gosling/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Dybantsa, guarding Tatum for the first time, admitted the assignment was a challenge, as was defending Tatum's new running mate, Paul George, who scored 28 points on 11-for-20 shooting.

In his mind, and now from experience, there's only so much Dybantsa can do against those two.

"At the end of the day, Jayson Tatum, Paul George, they are who they are," Dybantsa said. "They're gonna get shots up, but it's about making it tough. We don't want them just coming off a ball screen, getting a wide-open three, getting them uncomfortable, getting them out of rhythm. But they're gonna make shots. They're All-Stars, they're future Hall of Famers, but just trying to make it tough on them."

Tatum got the better of Dybantsa twice. First, he slipped free off a Sam Hauser screen for an uncontested dunk. Then he attacked Dybantsa's closeout from the perimeter and finished with a right-handed layup.

Fighting through Boston's screens troubled the Wizards all night long, Dybantsa included. For the rookie, it was a reminder of how much work remains before he's where he wants to be.

"I wanna be one of the better defenders in this league, and I can't just be dying on screens," Dybantsa said. "I gotta contest and get over the screen."

After the final buzzer, Tatum shared a handshake and hug with the former camper he once mentored years ago. He leaned in to say a few words, then patted Dybantsa on the chest and headed off.

They'll meet again in less than three weeks.

#2645. Donny Schatz Returns To The Dome With Hunt The Front

Donny Schatz, a 10-time World of Outlaws Sprint Car Series champion, is finally behind the wheel again. He will make his Gateway Dirt Nationals debut this December driving for Hunt The Front. The 49-year-old driver from Fargo, North Dakota, pilots a Traxxas-sponsored No. 15 Longhorn Chassis. This event marked his initial appearance in a Dirt Late Model nearly three and a half years ago. He teams up with Joseph Joiner for the event running December 3 through 5. The driver, who spent years as a car owner on the sidelines, is now making the move.

Schatz was not always sure he could handle the pressure of the indoor spectacle. He managed entries for his nieces, Amelia and Laela Eisenschenk, and later observed the event expand. He admitted to feeling unsure about his own skills during those years. "I said, 'Man, I'd love to go there and race, but I really don't know that I'm good enough to race it,'" Schatz recalled in an interview at Nov. 7's World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte, according to FloRacing.

Family ties keep pulling him back to the St. Louis Dome. His daughter Savanna and son-in-law Gordy Gundaker have deep roots in the event. Gundaker won a preliminary race at the Dome in 2017. The growing careers of Schatz's nieces also drive his return each December. "Kind of got me hooked there," Schatz said of Sheppard's performance. The event has become a regular part of his life, but this year he is the one competing.

Schatz landed this ride through a connection with team marketing director John Leonard. Their relationship goes back to when Leonard worked for CarQuest during Schatz's time at Tony Stewart Racing. The 18-year partnership with TSR ended in August 2025. "That car can go win this race. The team probably has a great opportunity to win this race, and I'd like to think that I do, too," Schatz said. He acknowledges the high bar for entry in this field. Saturday's finale will have six starting spots; the top three finishers in each of the two preliminary programs will qualify, bringing the field to 130 entrants.

For any driver, simply making the main event would constitute a huge accomplishment. "Listen, there's great racers who have gone there for several years and not even been able to make the show," Schatz said.

#2644. Aaron Rodgers says Mike McCarthy slept through meetings, held a grudge

Buried in Aaron Rodgers' tirade against Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is a "concerned friend," the quarterback said.

On the Nov. 25 edition of "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers accused McCarthy of "unhealthy" behavior that led to the coach missing walkthroughs and falling asleep in meetings.

"How many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff?" Rodgers said "… This guy's calling the plays!"

Rodgers said he told McCarthy "we got to make a change" about the offensive play caller and voiced that opinion on behalf of team, who talked about McCarthy's behavior and absences, according to Rodgers.

"I covered for him for a lot of years and we worked around it," Rodgers said. "And if you're standing on the truth and the facts … it's all firsthand accounts of what actually happened."

Rodgers said he has known about McCarthy dating back to their time together with the Green Bay Packers from 2008-18. The only time it became contentious, he said, was when Rodgers confronted McCarthy about his habits after the 2014 NFC championship game and after the a loss to the Buffalo Bills during the 2018 regular season. McCarthy was fired midway through that campaign; Rodgers said a staff member told him that McCarthy had said he had not forgiven Rodgers for "getting him fired in 2018."

"What he's saying and what he's actually doing is completely different," Rodgers said. "Anybody in the facility with nothing to lose would tell you the exact same thing.

"Nobody knew that this was going on for ten years in Green Bay."

Rodgers lamented that the Steelers are 6-4 and currently occupy the seventh seed in the AFC playoff race. Pittsburgh has lost two games in a row during which the offense looked borderline incompetent.

The final straw and impetus to go public with his qualms, Rodgers said, was an incident at halftime of the most recent loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Trailing 13-3, according to Rodgers, McCarthy broke down the huddle with "one, two, three ... Packers!"

Rodgers told McAfee that he told McCarthy that he wants him to step away and work on his health or focus on the high-level jobs of a head coach and leave the offense and play calling to the assistants and Rodgers.

Their conversations did not necessarily end on a good note, he said. Tight end Pat Freiermuth called Rodgers to express his bewilderment that Rodgers was inactive when the four-time MVP learned of the news himself. Mason Rudolph will start Friday Nov. 27 against the Denver Broncos.

Other individuals who have talked to McCarthy "about some of these habits," Rodgers said, and did not respond well.

#2642. Putting Phoenix’s four-game winning streak into perspective

The Phoenix Suns have fought and clawed their way back above .500, and as they sit at 9-7 preparing to face the Houston Rockets in NBA Cup play tonight, one common question is being asked: Are they legit, or are they simply beating up on bad teams?

This is one of those situations where I feel like multiple things can be true at once. Yes, the Suns have gotten right during a valley in their competition's quality. And I would certainly take these results over dropping a game or two against subpar competition, something we've become all too familiar with in recent years. Many would find themselves stewing had they dropped a game to Utah or were defeated by the Kings.

How legit are they? Time will ultimately tell. I look at it through this lens: Where did you predict the Suns would finish the season? The majority of Bright Side readers had them falling somewhere in the 44 to 47 win range. At 9-7? They're on pace for 46 wins.

So, despite the interesting journey to get to this point, the Suns are kind of exactly who we thought they were. They're a team that most certainly has flaws, possesses the ability to be competitive, and can win games. They reside somewhere between the NBA's elite teams and the basement dwellers.

What we've witnessed thus far is a reminder that the journey to whatever the final record may be isn't linear. It's one defined by peaks and valleys, opportunities presented by the schedule, and those unfortunate back-to-backs against quality competition where it feels like you're being set up to lose. How many times did we play Oklahoma City or San Antonio last season on the second night of a back-to-back, am I right?

Tonight's game against Houston will be an interesting one, considering the Rockets enter at 13-5 and possess one of the best offenses in the league. And should the Suns lose? Many will sprint to their keyboards, overreact to the result, and begin questioning the current state of the Phoenix Suns. I'd advise against that. Remember that this journey is a long and winding road, and for a team that resides somewhere in the middle, those results are to be expected.

The Suns don't need to prove they're a championship contender tonight. They need to keep building, keep finding ways to win, and continue showing that the team we thought could compete is, in fact, capable of competing. A loss to Houston wouldn't erase the progress they've made. A win would certainly add another layer of intrigue to the conversation.

But let's be honest. If they beat the Rockets, I'm not interested in hearing about strength of schedule anymore. Clear the parade route. We're winning a championship.

#2639. Why was Amad Diallo’s equaliser against Sporting disallowed?

Manchester United were furious as Amad Diallo's equaliser against Sporting was disallowed for a foul in the build-up.

Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad.

The United winger saw his shot saved by Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira but he followed in to head the ball into an empty net.

Sporting v Man United LIVE: Latest Champions League score and updates

The goal could not be reviewed because the referee had already given a foul (PA)

However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene.

Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad.

Tielemans was also booked by Marciniak for protesting.

United's players were seen remonstrating with referee Marciniak, who took charge of the 2022 World Cup final, as they left the pitch at half time.

It came after Mauricio Pochettino saw his new defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes in a shambolic first-half spell.

The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg.

If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left.

But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box.

Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row.

It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season.

#2638. 2027 Browns mock draft: Selecting a potential turkey at quarterback

The Cleveland Browns have surprisingly played themselves into the AFC playoff race, sitting one game behind the Cincinnati Bengals for first in the AFC North.

Playing meaningful games rather than focusing on draft position is a refreshing change of pace for the franchise. But it does not erase the reality that the Browns will be rebuilding the quarterback room in 2027.

Just what that remodeling will look like is still in the "to be determined" file, as the Browns could:

Run it back with the current group (not at all likely).

Decide it is time to unleash Shedeur Sanders as the starter on an unsuspecting NFL (literally not happening).

Some mix of the always popular veteran "bridge quarterback" to pair with a rookie selected in the 2027 NFL Draft. (Quite possible, even if that bridge is current starter Deshaun Watson, which no one would have seen coming a few months ago).

That final bullet point brings us to a mock draft from Nate Tice at Yahoo Sports, which, unfortunately, has the Browns embracing the Thanksgiving spirit by selecting a potential turkey at the quarterback position.

Tice projects the Browns to be selecting at No. 17 (with the selection they received from the Los Angeles Rams as part of the Myles Garrett trade) and No. 20 (with their own pick).

With that first selection, Tice embraces the "Browns is the Browns" mantra by selecting South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers:

The Browns throw another dart at the quarterback position. And boy, what a chance of hitting the bull's-eye this would be. Sellers is young (important to the Browns process) and has some of the loudest tools you'll ever see at the position. His play has felt calmer and more decisive over the past month, but he will need more time, especially in a more conducive situation than the one he's been in the past few years. Landing in Cleveland with the Browns' exciting young group of pass catchers isn't the worst place to settle, especially with head coach Todd Monken, who has gotten the most out of his quarterbacks at multiple stops.

Sellers is one of the most divisive college quarterbacks, which is saying a lot given the expected draft class. While athletic, he has only completed 63.1 percent of his career passes, while most top quarterbacks surpass 70 percent. He tosses interceptions (23), which are not really balanced out by just 50 touchdown passes.

Sellers is a quarterback who will have big games, like his four-touchdown performance this season against Florida – but offset that with clunkers, like completing 56 percent of his passes against Tennessee or throwing for just 87 yards against Georgia.

The Browns have searched so long for a quarterback, and made a mess of it far too often, that it is hard to see how selecting a player who is going to need a year (or likely more) to develop, with no guarantee of success.

Three picks later, Tice adds some depth to the defense with the selection of Notre Dame defensive end Boubacar Traore:

I peeked at another offensive lineman here, despite this year's Spencer Fano selection, and hit on the Austin Barber pick. Funnily enough, I have compared Traore to Jared Verse (but might be leaning more toward a DeMarcus Lawrence comparison). Either way, those are two strong defenders who can push the pocket, and that's exactly what Traore brings to the table. He would be another strong edge defender to add to the Browns' front.

The Browns can always use help on defense, and in 32 career games, Traore has 88 tackles, 15.5 sacks, and 26.5 tackles for loss. His draft stock has been rising this season, and if the Irish make a run through the college football playoffs, Traore will have plenty of opportunities to showcase his talent against tougher competition than the likes of Rice, Navy, and Purdue.

So there you have it. The Browns "throw another dart" at the quarterback position and add some help for the defensive line with a player who might be Jared Verse 2.0.

#2635. NBA announces $11 billion investment to build European arenas for new league

The NBA has unveiled a $11 billion funding initiative aimed at developing and renovating basketball arenas across Europe. This investment is designed to support the launch of the new NBA and FIBA-created European League that could see its inaugural tip-off as soon as next fall.

On Wednesday, Nov. 25, the NBA announced a detailed strategic partnership with a coalition of leading global investment firms, including Apollo Sports Capital, Ares Management, Arctos, Blackstone, HPS Investment Partners, J.P. Morgan and others. These firms will spearhead the funding initiative, collaborating closely with participating clubs, team owners, local developers and a range of service providers. Together, they aim to construct and upgrade world-class basketball arenas.

According to the NBA, the initiative will "provide prospective clubs and ownership groups with access to sustainable capital and the NBA's expertise to develop modern arena facilities and, where appropriate, surrounding districts."

More: NBA power rankings: How far will slumping Thunder, Celtics fall?

The NBA and FIBA have also emphasized that this initiative represents a significant investment not only in the sport itself, but also in the economic vitality of host cities. New or renovated arenas are expected to drive local growth and create jobs.

"We've seen firsthand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. "As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside FIBA, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events."

While official host cities have yet to be announced, the NBA-FIBA project is reportedly considering several countries as prime candidates for the new league.

Potential host cities include London and Manchester (Britain), Paris and Lyon (France), Madrid and Barcelona (Spain), Rome and Milan (Italy), Munich and Berlin (Germany), Athens (Greece) and Istanbul (Turkey).

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: NBA announces $11 billion investment to build European arenas for new league

#2632. WWE Survivor Series 2026 predictions: Will The Rock and Cody Rhodes turn WrestleMania season upside down?

Survivor Series: WarGames, WWE's final "Big Four" premium live event of 2026, goes down this weekend in Houston.

Although the event has shifted in recent years to be headlined by "the match beyond," this year's edition will also feature a traditional five-on-five Survivor Series match between Team USA and Team Mexico. In addition to the in-ring action, WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson will make an appearance on the show, leaving the wrestling world buzzing about a potential return to the ring for "The Final Boss."

With so much to dissect heading into Survivor Series: WarGames, the Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — have gathered to break down all the angles and make predictions for the event.

Riggs: It's really difficult to say. Honestly, after seeing John Cena break the fourth wall into a million pieces recently, I could totally see Rock returning literally just to say something nice in a reflective, nothing-promo about his WWE career. Given how Saturday's appearance has been advertised, that outcome feels likely — at a minimum.

Whether he returns a second time on the show is another question.

Ideally, I think he should, and it should come after 946 beats the Bloodline, with Roman Reigns taking the pin. As the only man you can put ahead of Reigns "at the table," Rock should walk out to feign being supportive, but instead be disappointed that his family (Reigns specifically) failed in this "war" and failed the family as a whole. He hits Reigns with a Rock Bottom as the rest of the crew stares in disbelief, but refuses to do anything because, again, Rock is the only guy above Reigns.

That sets up their eventual "SaudiMania" dream match that's been wanted for years — ideally, again, with Reigns dropping the title to Oba Femi before then.

Rock vs. Reigns doesn't need the title. Just put the "Ufa Lafa," as LA Knight once said, on the line and call it good. This is too easy, which is why WWE won't do it, sadly.

Jackman: I'm betting on The Rock springing a Hall of Fame surprise on John Cena. The WWE Hall of Fame ceremony has lacked that star power over the past few years and immortalizing the 17-time champion is the perfect way to fix that. Just as importantly for TKO, Cena's involvement in the Hall of Fame will also help put some shine on SaudiMania, just at the moment that they need to start thinking seriously about that show.

I really don't think you can overestimate how much WWE is going to need to throw at next year's 'Mania, both in terms of making the show sparkle and winning back the goodwill of fans after selling the company's landmark event to the highest bidder in the first place. Putting Cena in the Hall of Fame will be a decent start on that front.

As for what I'd like to happen, I don't think I differ from the very markiest of internet marks on this one. I want to see Dwayne Johnson actually play that Final Boss "character" he likes to opine about on podcasts and give us the next installment of this long-running story arc that shaped both WrestleMania XL and WrestleMania 41. The man has unfinished business with both Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns, and we shouldn't ever let that rest.

Is The Rock vs. Roman Reigns still on the table for 2027? (WWE, Getty Images)

Sulla-Heffinger: I like Drake's idea of The Rock coming out twice during the show. There needs to be some kind of acknowledgment of the fact that he debuted at Survivor Series 30 years ago, so I would imagine you see more of the Dwayne Johnson side of The Rock's character open the show — perhaps with John Cena in a major moment to announce the next participant in the John Cena Classic — to really build up buzz for the night.

Assuming the men's WarGames matchup closes the show, in my ideal world we get the "Final Boss" delivering a Rock Bottom to Roman Reigns and setting up the main event of Night 2 of WrestleMania 43. Aside from the obvious big-money match between Rock and Reigns, this program would also free up The Usos, Jacob Fatu and Solo Sikoa to pursue other stories — The Bloodline can remain a faction, but we don't need to see them involved in each others' business ALL of the time. Rock-Reigns is big enough that it makes sense to have the rest of the Bloodline not pick sides. A loss to 946 and the threat of The Rock builds in some much-needed vulnerability that allows Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship run to end — whether that be to Oba Femi or Penta.

Dansby: In an ideal world, Rocky leaves the in-ring work to the full-time superstars. We're now 25 years removed from The Rock's prime as a professional wrestler, and the novelty of seeing him return has long worn off. The Roman Reigns vs. The Rock "dream match" is five years past due at this point and should be left in the "what-if" category. Not every dream match needs to become a reality, especially when it comes at the expense of the stars carrying the company today.

Ideally, The Rock shows up, announces an attendance record, promotes his latest movie and fades into the background. The last thing WWE needs is another WrestleMania season dictated by The Rock's availability, especially if it means taking away Oba Femi's EARNED spot in the upcoming WrestleMania main event.

Jackman: I'm going with the ringleader here.

From the minute Royce Keys made the jump to WWE at the Royal Rumble, the company has consistently presented him as a star in waiting. The cynical part of me wonders if they have an extra incentive to give a larger push to these AEW-to-WWE switchers. That has definitely been the case for Penta and Jade Cargill, for example, both of whom have been given the red-carpet treatment since they decided to jump ship from Tony Khan's roster to the clutches of TKO. Royce Keys could well be the next person to get that rub,

Obviously, the fact that Keys is already in command position going into WarGames makes him the easy pick, but he's still the right call — particularly when all signs point to him going one-on-one with Roman Reigns before long. A PLE showdown with "The Tribal Chief" is about as serious of a layup as you can get in WWE right now. Even if the chances of anyone not named Oba Femi beating Roman are close to zero.

Royce Keys (L) has made a much larger impact in WWE than many expected.

Riggs: Cruz Montana may still be the freshest face in the group, but after only one match, there's something about the guy that just feels right.

Don't get me wrong, Royce Keys has been great. I still think the whole genesis of this feud was pretty dumb, corny, and unexplained in certain beats, but thankfully they're all talented enough to have made it work. Now it's just a matter of what WWE does with the group after this, because they've been booked into that corner of dominance where anything but a win on Saturday absolutely crushes this stable.

Nonetheless, I think in a group or breaking away, Montana might be the guy to last the longest as a notable player.

Sulla-Heffinger: In the near-term, it's hard to not go with the faction's leader in Royce Keys. In terms of being the most credible main-event level talent in the group, Keys has been building toward this on the main roster since his debut in WWE.

That said, I think Cruz Montana is the person we'll be talking about coming out of this match and is someone who has thrived as a singles performer in his most recent runs with TNA and in NXT. I liken his expected rise to what we've seen with Jacob Fatu — he's got a swagger and charisma about him that makes him impossible not to like as that tweener-style babyface/heel.

Dansby: Why do we have to pit these guys against each other? How about they all go on to have bright futures? The beauty of this faction is that each member can benefit from its success without necessarily having to follow the same career trajectory. The 946 is the perfect vehicle to establish Royce Keys as a main-event player, while Carmelo Hayes is in a prime position to break out in the mid-card before eventually becoming his own man in a year or so.

A babyface Hayes feuding with former members of the 946 in 2028 will feed families. In the meantime, the other members have an opportunity to establish their individual identities, find their respective places on the roster and thrive. A successful faction should create multiple stars, not just serve as a launching pad for one.

That's not Becky's fault. She's a great person to have at the helm, as always. But the women's roster booking, in particular, has been in the absolute gutter this year. For starters, we can improve things by disbanding The Judgment Day and shuffling up each brand a bit. Give new people a chance. Until then, nothing will change, and these feuds will keep dragging, floundering, and repeating in borderline identical fashions.

Dansby: Will The Judgment Day ever end? WWE has been teasing the group's breakup for three years now, and we're still waiting for a meaningful payoff.

Putting the championship back on Becky Lynch would just be spinning the wheels on something we've already seen half a dozen times. Becky is an established star, but another championship reign doesn't necessarily solve the lack of creativity surrounding the title picture.

Instead, how about Liv retains the championship and eventually drops it to Roxanne Perez at the Royal Rumble? There's already a natural storyline there, and it would give WWE an opportunity to elevate one of its brightest young talents while finally moving The Judgment Day's story forward. Build the future, don't recycle the past.

Liv Morgan (R) and Becky Lynch collide Saturday for the Women's World Championship.

Jackman: Like Drake, I'm going to say no — albeit with apologies to Becky Lynch. I've said consistently in our power rankings that she's been the standard-setter in terms of the women's roster on "Raw," but even her abundant charisma can't save that division overnight. The Women's World Championship has had a dire run this year, seesawing back and forth between the same two names without any zest or creativity whatsoever.

Can you name one memorable moment, in-ring or otherwise, from this perma-feud between Liv Morgan and Stephanie Vaquer? OK, let me rephrase that … can you name one memorable moment that isn't that horrible head-to-head collision that had everyone wincing for weeks afterward. I rate both performers highly, but they've just had zero chemistry between them. I suppose a Becky win would break that deadlock, but I just don't have confidence right now it would fix anything long-term.

Sulla-Heffinger: Yes, and it's a move that needs to happen. Morgan seemed primed for a massive 2026 after winning the Royal Rumble (finally), but her title reigns have been remarkably unremarkable — due to a lack of defenses — and the Judgment Day has lost seemingly all of its luster beyond just being an interference vehicle for the Women's World Champion.

Another Lynch championship reign would bring freshness to the main-event picture on "Raw" and she's still among the best WWE has on the microphone. There's a depth that Lynch brings to any feud she's in, and it would be a fitting moment during Survivor Series season, which is where we saw her full transformation into "The Man" after she was bloodied by Nia Jax eight years ago.

Sulla-Heffinger: Only when it's thrown together for the sake of being thrown together, like we've seen in recent years.

Elimination Chamber and Money in the Bank work on their own as PLEs because there's a reward attached to them. WarGames, like steel cage and Hell in a Cell matches, needs to have a personal rivalry in order to really be captivating. Having violence and stipulations just for the sake of having violence and stipulations cheapens the experience for everyone involved.

Jackman: WarGames suffers from the perennial curse of the team vs. team gimmick match, in that everything ends up being dictated by the need to fill the two warring teams in the first place. It's a classic case of the tail wagging the dog.

When you have a strong faction, you don't notice so much. The first Bloodline run was a solid example of that, even if the opposition team was a bit random, as was the Judgment Day match in 2023. By contrast, my interest in last year's main event suffered from the fact that it was built around The Vision — a faction that had been losing steam for months at that point, thanks to back-to-back injuries and a general lack of imagination.

Of course that's still miles better than the women's side, where the lineups are so random that they might as well be drawn from a sorting hat most years. I mean, half of this year's participants have been "announced" via run-ins, without any plausible backstory. Honestly, it makes you yearn for the days of Damage CTRL.

I'd also question whether WarGames is really as good as we all hoped. We've had eight of these matches on the main roster now, and the memorable moments are pretty thin on the ground. I know it's a bit sacrilegious to express doubts about a Dusty Rhodes creation, but it's hard to see what the "double ring and mega-cage" setup really adds. Then there is the staggered entry thing, where you just end up waiting for the last entrant so the match can actually begin.

WarGames is once again a Bloodline affair this year.

Dansby: I still enjoy WarGames. The build to this year's men's match has been well executed, and the women's match always delivers its share of fun and memorable moments. What I'm particularly happy about, though, is the return of the traditional five-on-five Survivor Series elimination match to accompany WarGames rather than having one stipulation completely replace the other.

We've seen how entertaining the process of recruiting five superstars for a team can be, especially when you have to navigate existing rivalries, conflicting personalities and uneasy alliances. There's plenty of storytelling potential in the traditional Survivor Series format, both in the weeks leading up to the event and during the match itself. I'd love for WWE to continue incorporating both stipulations moving forward.

Riggs: Completely. It feels like I've been saying this every week in the recaps. The PLE gimmick has completely ruined a match like this. It needs to be dictated by the story and not the event.

The same goes for something like Hell In A Cell. You could even argue Elimination Chamber. But you don't need any more evidence than the painfully absurd conglomeration matches we see annually in the women's matches. WWE couldn't care less about putting something interesting together for those matches. It's just people being thrown together entirely out of the blue. (Hi, Stephanie Vaquer!) At least they try with the men, I guess.

Jackman: This storyline has been a bit of a sleeper hit, hasn't it? When they first announced the whole Team USA vs. Team Mexico idea, on Stephanie McMahon's podcast of all places, I figured it was just a cute attempt to get some cheap pops from the Texas crowd (which should be nicely divided across both camps). Now we have this more intriguing subplot involving Rhodes, Punk and Rollins that gives us a reason to actually engage our brains a bit more.

Compared to the rest of the card, I'm actually pretty excited to see where it goes. Saturday will be almost exactly three years since CM Punk's return, when you had Seth Rollins plotzing and cursing in the aisle, and this seems the perfect callback to that moment. Let's see whether it leads to a full-on brawl between Punk and Rhodes, who clearly have unfinished business after their first outing at SummerSlam.

I should declare an interest here as one of the folks who remains resolutely behind the idea of a Cody heel turn. I still think that dark Cody beating CM Punk at next year's WrestleMania is a risk worth taking — whether it's for the title or not.

Riggs: It should be. You can't just drop these hints and not come through.

Well, OK, we know that's not true at all — WWE has dropped countless potential angles over the years without follow-ups. It'd be a real shame to do so with a Rhodes turn, though. The pro-wrestling world has wanted it for ages, and he'd be phenomenal in the role at this stage. Also, Rhodes being on the outside looking in for a title shot carves a perfect path to bring him back into the scene without adding more Rhodes fatigue.

Sulla-Heffinger: Yes, and it should come in a victorious effort for Team USA. This story has been built with Punk stealing the limelight from Rhodes, so it only makes sense for Punk to pick up the win for his team and have everyone celebrate with him before Rhodes hits a CrossRhodes and turning in the process. I suspect it will get a huge pop from the crowd, since a large portion of the wrestling world has been clamoring for this change for a while.

With jealousy being the driving force behind Rhodes' turn, it's already got a leg up on John Cena's turn from last year. The initial turn may not carry the same shock value of Cena's, Seth Rollins' or Hulk Hogan's, but Rhodes' motivation for it allows the decision to make sense and Punk being beloved should prevent it from flaming out.

Dansby: Heel turn or no heel turn, can we all agree that Team Mexico HAS to win this match? I don't care if Cody turns heel, if Seth Rollins and CM Punk can coexist, or if the egos on Team USA ultimately lead to their downfall. There's enough star power and overlapping storylines on that team for everyone involved to remain relevant regardless of the outcome.

What I don't want is for Team Mexico to become a supporting cast in a story centered entirely around Team USA's dysfunction. Give the Mexican superstars their moment and allow them to benefit from sharing the ring with some of WWE's biggest names. However we get there, I just need to see Team Mexico standing tall at the end of this match.

Men's WarGames match: The Bloodline vs. The 946 (Dansby, Jackman, Riggs, Sulla-Heffinger)

Women's WarGames match: Charlotte Flair, Tatum Paxley, Alexa Bliss, Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer (Dansby, Jackman, Riggs, Sulla-Heffinger) vs. Fatal Influence, Jade Cargill and Michin

Women's World Championship match: Liv Morgan (Dansby, Jackman) vs. Becky Lynch (Riggs, Sulla-Heffinger)

5-on-5 Survivor Series Match: Team USA (Jackman, Riggs, Sulla-Heffinger) vs. Team Mexico (Dansby)

#2630. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

Running back Saquon Barkley, defensive tackle Jalen Carter, tight end Dallas Goedert, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith are also without designations after appearing on the injury report this week.

#2627. 2026-27 NBA Minutes Report: Brandon Ingram returns, Cameron Boozer is sidelined, more

Welcome to the NBA Minutes Report. Every week, I will review each team's updated minutes per game to see which players are seeing the court more or less than in previous weeks and what their impact has been. That can help you with any fantasy basketball decisions you may need to make, but also help you get a lay of the land on what's happening around the NBA and which players are gaining or losing value.

The charts below are also great for exploring on your own. You can track the minutes over the last three, five, ten games, and for the entire season, to see which trends stand out to you. All of this data was made accessible by Kyle Bland, who is incredibly talented and also extremely generous. Be sure to follow him to check out all of his baseball data as well.

We've now seen a full week with CJ McCollum (calf) on the bench, and that's given us slightly more minutes for Corey Kispert(who had 18 points on Sunday) and Lu Dort. However, most of the minutes are just going to the starters. Jock Landale has also been nursing a hip injury, which has created an opportunity for Zuby Ejiofor to enter the rotation.

Mitchell Robinson has been dealing with an illness, but his time in Boston has not gone well. In fact, things are not going well in Boston overall. They beat the Wizards on Tuesday, but had lost four straight games before that, including losses to the Kings and Warriors. Derrick White's shooting has been an issue again this season, and the Celtics just aren't consistently getting strong production from their best unit either.

Sadly, Nolan Traore suffered a hamstring injury that's going to sideline him for a few months. The Nets are likely going to spread playing time around for their young players, but Mikel Brown Jr. got 29 minutes on Monday and scored 17 points with five rebounds and seven assists. He also had six turnovers, but he's gonna have the ball in his hands far more often. The rest of the fill-in players aren't overly interesting.

Kon Knueppel, Grayson Allen, and Dennis Schroder all remain sidelined, so Sion James continues to start and play big minutes. There's not a ton of production, but he's a role player. Christian Anderson scored 25 points in 25 minutes on Monday, and this was a bit of a "hot hand" situation, but there aren't that many options off the bench right now. The rest of the bench totaled just six points in that game.

As we mentioned last week, we've slowly started to see Nic Claxton's minutes tick up. He played 23 in a win over the Cavaliers on Monday but had sat out the game against the Nuggets before. Norman Powell is now dealing with a hamstring injury, so Buddy Hield has stepped into the starting lineup and had 17 points and five rebounds in 27 minutes in that game on Monday. He is going to shoot when he's on the court.

Evan Mobley remains sidelined with a toe injury, which has shortened the Cavs' rotation. Sam Merrill is starting, and Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor have become the two key contributors off the bench. The rest is pretty much status quo here, and the usage sits heavily with the starters.

Caleb Martin's role continues to grow as a starter in Dallas. He played 30 minutes in their win over the Nuggets on Tuesday, scoring 13 points with four rebounds, four assists, and five steals. He's been a great complement to scorers like Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. Morez Johnson Jr. has also clearly earned the backup big man role, ahead of Santi Aldama.

The Nuggets had been playing well before their loss to the Mavericks, and a lot of that has to do with how elite Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray are as a duo, which I covered in a video this week. The Nuggets also have a clear-cut starting five, and then like to use Spencer Jones as their sixth man, but the rest of the bench is a rotating group that all seems ot play around 10-17 minutes depending on the matchup.

Cade Cunningham missed Tuesday's win over the Magic with a knee injury, which led to 35 minutes for Daniss Jenkins. We also saw Isaiah Joe start and play 30 minutes in that win, scoring 21 points with four rebounds. He seems to be settling into a larger role now that he's back from injury and Duncan Robinson is still out. The Pistons need his ability to space the floor.

The Warriors have deepened their rotation in the wake of all their injuries, but also 6-7 players are really playing meaningful minutes. Gui Santos did play 23 minutes in a win over the Celtics on Sunday, but that was because he was having a solid game overall. We finally saw De'Anthony Melton play 27 minutes in that game, but he was 0-7 from the field. Charles Bassey has become the starting center and had 13 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals in that win over the Celtics. He's been pretty good for Golden State.

The Rockets run one of the tightest rotations in basketball, and not much has changed with it over the last week. In fact, they don't have a single player listed on the injury report.

T.J. McConnell is dealing with a hamstring injury, which has led to more time for Braden Smith, who started and played 24 minutes in Monday's game against the Thunder. Jalen Slawson also played 20 minutes in that game and scored 16 points with 10 rebounds and four blocks, which is insane production in that many minutes. He could earn a larger role for himself.

We saw Brandon Ingram make his season debut on Monday night, which I recorded a video about. That led to a decrease in minutes for Max Strus and Gradey Dick, and Dick could be out of the rotation entirely. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser also returned to the court, which has pushed Isaiah Jackson down the pecking order.

Austin Reaves remains out with a heel injury, so Quentin Grimes and Matisse Thybulle remain in key roles in this rotation. Jake LaRavia has been in the starting lineup and off the bench, but he still pushes 30 minutes a night, and the rest of the team has had sporadic production off the bench. It's a solid bench, but there isn't really one guy they lean on constantly, apart from knowing that Collin Sexton is going to get up shots when he's in the game.

Sadly, the big news in Memphis was that Cameron Boozer will be sidelined for at least a month with a sprained ankle. With Jerami Grant and GG Jackson also hurt, there are some questions about the depth on the wing in Memphis, all of which I discussed in a video this week.

The Heat are starting to figure some things out. They beat the Thunder on Sunday for their seventh win in a row, and that was without Giannis Antetokounmpo, who missed with a groin injury. Bobby Portis Jr. started for him, but he'll move back to the bench on Wednesday with Giannis back. We have seen Ryan Conwell take on a much bigger role off the bench, playing at least 26 minutes in each of the last five games.

The Bucks are really not good and have just two wins this season. Of course, one of them happened in their last game against the Raptors. They essentially used just an eight-man rotation in that game, with Nate Ament, Kel'el Ware, and Brayden Burries as the only bench players playing over eight minutes. Burries has been a tremendous success for the Bucks so far this season, and there's some freedom for him in coming off the bench and just playing with his hair on fire.

The Timberwolves continue to play well with Anthony Edwards sidelined, and a big reason for that is Jaden McDaniels. LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu have done a good job approximating Edwards' offensive value, but I think McDaniels may be the most important player on Minnesota right now, and I recorded a video discussing why he should make the All-Star Game.

We've now seen an extended period of time after Dejounte Murray demanded a trade, and Jeremiah Fears has unsurprisingly seen his role grow. Trey Murphy III will also play plenty of minutes, but he's not as much of a high-usage player as the other two. Saddiq Bey and Jordan Poole are the key pieces off the bench and fill flash, as they did on Monday against the Suns, but the production is not consistent.

The early-season struggles for Mikail Bridges and Josh Hart seem to be a little bit more in the rearview, and both players are trending back to their old roles with the Knicks finding their footing. OG Anunoby missed Sunday's game with a calf injury, which allowed Landry Shamet to start and Jose Alvarado to play 22 minutes off the bench, but it's not expected to be a long-term injury.

The Thunder lost Alex Caruso to a hip injury in addition to the larger injuries to Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, and Jalen Williams. As a result, Bennett Stirtz has seen his role grow. The production has been inconsistent, but the minutes might be there in the short term. Aday Mara missed Monday's game with a shin bruise, but he has been tremendous as a starter and figures to be a key part of this lineup for much of the season.

Domantas Sabonis still remains the most well-rounded offensive option on the offense, and Darius Acuff Jr. will have big games with his high usage role, but Keegan Murray is really struggling with his shot this year, and this just isn't an exciting team.

We've now seen a full week with Dylan Harper sidelined by a hip injury. That has, as expected, led to a slight minutes boost for Julian Champagnie and both Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant getting a few more minutes at night depending on the matchup.

Things are not going well for the Raptors, as evidenced by their loss to the Bucks on Monday. Kawhi Leonard (knee) and RJ Barrett (hamstring) remain out, but Scott Barnes is back to his normal role, which is big, and Collin Murray-Boyles finally returned from a concussion on Monday. Allen Graves and Ja'Kobe Walter have been playing more minutes lately, but there's not a lot of production coming along with it.

Jaxson Hayes had been playing meaningful minutes in the wake of Utah's many injuries, but he suffered a knee injury of his own. Svi Mykhailiuk has also seen a bigger role as a shooter off the bench, but he went just 1-7 from the field on Monday after a big night the game before, so it's hard to see him as a consistent option.

The Wizards have an incredibly narrow rotation right now. Only seven players played more than eight minutes in their loss to the Celtics on Tuesday. #2623. Chamblee Says PGA Tour Must Cut Safety Nets For LIV Returnees

Brandel Chamblee believes the PGA Tour must end its safety nets immediately. The analyst wants players who left for LIV Golf to lose their exemptions and prove they still belong. The analyst's approach removes the idea that past glory guarantees a future spot on the main tour.

The 2028 season will feature a new two-tier system on the PGA Tour. Players who jumped to the Saudi-backed circuit will face a harsh reality check. According to Chamblee's interview with Jimmy Roberts on The Big Swing, certain returning players could be required to compete on the Challenger Series or the Korn Ferry Tour. He argues that working back up the ladder is the only fair path forward.

Many former members of the tour secured strong positions for 2028 before leaving. Aaron Rai and Ryan Fox earned exemptions until 2031 after winning major championships. Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm are also expected to get spots in the Championship Series after serving one-year suspensions. These players won big events recently, yet Chamblee insists their past wins should not shield them now.

"I wouldn't be surprised if some of these players have got to go back to the Korn Ferry Tour, got to go to the [Challenger Series], and then work their way into the Championship Series, and as they should," Chamblee said. The analyst sees the current system as a flaw that lets players rest on laurels instead of competing for their jobs.

"You've got to come back and prove yourself," he added. "They've got a lot of safety nets on the PGA Tour. They should just do away with them." This stance challenges the tradition where long-time members keep their status regardless of current form.

The debate centers on what makes a player deserving of a spot. Chamblee argues that sports must answer why a specific person is playing over another. If the answer relies on something done five or ten years ago, the system has failed. He views the current exemptions as a convenience that hurts the competitive integrity of the game.

"If you really want to make golf more meritocratic, you need to get rid of these safety nets," Chamblee stated. "Sports should always be answering the question: why are you here versus somebody else? And if the answer is because you did something great five or 10 years ago, that is the wrong answer." This logic suggests that talent fades and effort must be constant.

The 2027 season is set to be very interesting as the tour prepares for these structural shifts. Marco Penge nearly lost his card at The RSM Classic but secured a spot in the top 100. His struggle highlights the pressure on players to perform now rather than rely on history.

"I think people look back and at least over the last 40 or 50 years, remember this is probably the worst period in golf's history and I'm not so sure that it won't echo unfortunately into the future," Chamblee warned, according to GolfMagic. The damage from the split could last for decades if the sport does not fix its rules.
